_comment: SPARK — S176 P1: THE VOLTKIN HIMSELF, AS ART RATHER THAN AS A PUPPET.
Owner, S176: "do Voltkin. So make him attack and die with the new art I generated for him. Make
him run. Make him idle. Make him ... the whole loop of him and what he's supposed to do. Very
consistent and coherent and looking awesome, especially with the TV building."
⛔ WHAT THIS REPLACES, AND IT IS NOT AN ANIMATION BUG. The Voltkin has never been drawn from a
sheet. He is a procedural Pixi.Graphics puppet (`voltkinPose` -> `drawVoltkin`, S106) with a
TWO-STILL sprite layer over it (S110: voltkin-idle.png / voltkin-zap.png). The atlas path in
`voltkinFrames.ts` was retired in S107 and its manifest kept only as a tested spec. So he has
exactly two pictures and no loop at all — which is the whole of what the owner is seeing.
⛔ THE CLIPS ARE THE ONES HE GENERATED IN S173. Nothing newer exists on disk: every file in this
folder is dated 2026-09-12, verified by mtime at the start of S176. "The new art I generated" IS
these four clips. COST OF THIS FILE: $0.00 — no veo call was made.
⭐ EVERY WINDOW BELOW IS MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. `check-clip.mjs` was run, and then its own
detector was re-run over EVERY frame rather than its 24 samples, because the 24-sample verdict is
wrong on two of these four clips:
· idle — check-clip PASSES it ("bars present throughout, the stable case the packer handles,
no action needed"). ⛔ THAT IS A FALSE PASS. It tests whether bars are PRESENT in every
sampled frame, never whether their WIDTH is constant. idle's bars ramp 318 -> 104 across
f0..f7 and are constant at 104 only from f8. Sampling at stride 4 sees "barred" in all 24
and calls it stable. A sampleStart IS needed; the packer would otherwise average a content
column across a ramp and crop every frame wrong.
· walk — the prior session's `sampleStart:36` verdict is CORRECT and is now proven rather than
repeated: frames 36..71 carry zero amputation and zero bars, and the only amputated frames in
the clip (72, 79, 86, 87) fall AFTER that window. The window below is tightened to 48..71,
the scale-stable subset (8.4% subject-height drift instead of the window's wider spread).
⛔ DIE IS A STILL, FOR THE SECOND TIME IN THIS REPO, AND FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN THE WOLF'S.
die.mp4's only amputation-free, scale-stable window is f44..55 — which is him STAGGERING with his
arms up, not dying. The actual sequence (collapse f57..63, corpse f66+) is edge-hit by the
lightning column, and from ~f75 the background turns GREY: the matte lifts near-WHITE only, so a
grey ground packs as a solid slab under the body. `voltkin-dead.png` is the owner's own drawn
corpse and is a better picture than any frame in the clip, for the same $0.
⚠ stillHeightRatio 0.581 = 412/709, MEASURED on alpha (subject bbox, not canvas) off the two
source PNGs so the poses are directly comparable. Sits alongside the shipped die rows: direwolf
0.621, hound 0.61, orcs 0.76. Do NOT exempt the still from normaliseStateScale instead — S175
shipped that and it came out ENORMOUS, because with no normalisation a still keeps the scale of
its own small canvas. Neither naive branch is right; the ratio is.
⚠ THE STILL IS `voltkin-dead-matted.png`, RGB ON 254-WHITE — never the transparent cut-out. A
transparent PNG stores see-through pixels as RGB 0,0,0, which the matte reads as SUBJECT and packs
the art inside a black box (protocol 4.1a).
⚠ SEPARATE SPEC FILE, deliberately. `atlas-specs.json` in this folder builds the TV BUILDING sheet,
which is shipped and green; the character is a different sheet with a different cell and must not
force a rebuild of it.

specs.name: voltkin
_why_framesPerState: ⭐⭐ OWNER RULING, S176, mid-priority - THE 12-FRAME DIAL IS CLOSED, AND UPWARDS. Verbatim:
"we have to cut out the video loops into many many ... last time you did twelve for some
bosses, and it didn't even look that good. So if you're gonna do less than twelve cutouts,
then we're definitely gonna not have it look good. It's gonna just be choppy and moving from
one stance to another too quickly." Every other sheet in this repo is 12; this is the first
at 20.
⛔ AND 20 IS A CEILING I MEASURED, NOT A NUMBER I LIKED. The atlas is ONE row of cells per
state, so its WIDTH is framesPerState x cellW. cellW here is 382 (the packer widens it to fit
walk's horizontal quadruped sprawl), so 20 frames = 7640 px and 24 frames = 9168 px. 8192 is
the conservative WebGL MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE floor on older and mobile GPUs; past it the sheet
does not merely look worse, it FAILS TO LOAD - and a failed atlas in this renderer is SILENT
(the catch drops to the procedural puppet), so the owner would see the old rig come back with
nothing in any log. The widest sheet shipped in this repo today is 6432 px (t9boss-nagas).
⭐ THE LEVER, IF HE WANTS MORE THAN 20: cellW is driven by the WALK row alone. A walk clip
framed upright rather than as a horizontal dash would drop cellW towards 256, which buys 32
frames inside the same ceiling. That is an ART change, not a packer setting.
⚠ SAMPLING IS NOW NEAR-NATIVE, which is the actual win: walk samples 20 of 24 source frames
and attack 20 of 26, i.e. almost every generated frame survives instead of every other one.
die is a still, so its 20 cells are 20 copies of one drawing - they cost PNG bytes (which
compress to nearly nothing, being identical) and buy no motion. The packer has no per-state
frame override; framesPerState is global.
_why_ticksPerFrame: ⚠ HALVED-ISH ALONGSIDE framesPerState, AND NOT COSMETICALLY. A row's wall-clock duration is
framesPerState x ticksPerFrame. Leaving the shipped 12-frame cadences (7/3/5/5) at 20 frames
would have stretched every loop by 67% - a slow-motion Voltkin - which is the opposite of the
owner's complaint. The new pairs hold the ORIGINAL durations and spend the extra frames on
⛔ attack 20x3 = 60 IS EXACT, AND IT HAS TO BE. VOLTKIN_ATTACK_CADENCE_TICKS is 60 and the
FIRE tick is 30; a row that outlasts the cadence re-triggers the swing before the animation
finishes drawing, which is the stutter S175 predicted for the enraged Warlord and fixed by
halving his frame rate with his cadence. 20x3 lands the row on the cadence boundary.

idle._why: Bars are constant at L104/R104 only from f8 (they ramp 318->104 across f0..f7), and subject height is flat at ~650-669 px across f24..f64 before it sags to ~600 as the aura dies down. f24..f63 is the stable, aura-carrying middle. check-clip's own verdict on this clip is a FALSE PASS - see the header.

walk._why: Bars ramp to zero by f35 and the clip is amputation-free from f36; f48..f71 is the scale-stable subset (8.4% height drift). The four amputated frames (72, 79, 86, 87) sit deliberately outside the window.

attack._why: ⛔ THE DISCHARGE WINDOW (f36..69) WAS PACKED FIRST, AUDITIONED ON THE DARK BOARD, AND REJECTED - and the measurement is why, not taste. Measuring the YELLOW BODY separately from the CYAN BOLTS: idle's body is 582 px; the attack clip is framed wider throughout, so its body is ~409 px in EVERY window. normaliseStateScale corrects that by comparing whole-subject heights - and the bolts ARE subject. In f36..69 the bolts double the extent (allH ~720 vs idle's 659), so the pass sees a correctly-sized subject, declines to scale, and the CHARACTER lands at 409/720 of the cell: he visibly HALVES the instant he attacks. It also widened cellW from 256 to 429 to fit the bolts, which every other row then pays for. In f70..95 the bolts are gone (allH 436), the pass scales x1.51, and the body lands at ~618 - within 6% of idle. That is the owner's "very consistent and coherent" made literal.
attack._why_no_bolts_in_the_sprite: ⭐ AND THE LIGHTNING IS NOT LOST, BECAUSE THE ENGINE ALREADY DRAWS IT. `creatureAttack` emits one ARC_FLASH per CREATURE_ATTACK dispatch - an arc from the creature to the target midpoint over ARC_FLASH_DURATION_TICKS (~300 ms) - plus screen-shake. Baking bolts into the sprite would double-draw the strike AND shrink him to do it. This is the same rule the project states for per-strike visuals: derive them every frame from synced state rather than ship them in the frame. f70..95 is his arms-raised slam pose, at full size, with the engine's own arc over it.
attack._the_one_line_to_change: If the owner wants the drawn bolts back, this is sampleStart 36 / sampleWindow 34 - and he will shrink. Nothing else needs touching.

die._why: See the header. The clip's only clean window is a stagger, not a death, and its corpse frames sit on a grey ground the near-white matte cannot lift.
